title: Seafood lasagne
subtitle: Prawn, crab, and salmon in a cream béchamel with fresh pasta
excerpt: Layers of fresh pasta, prawns, crab, and flaked salmon in a cream-enriched béchamel, finished with Parmesan and baked until golden. An Italian dinner-party dish that rewards the effort.
sourceNotes: Seafood lasagne (lasagne ai frutti di mare or lasagne ai sigilli) is a well-established Italian preparation found throughout coastal Lazio, Campania, and the Adriatic regions. The method of combining béchamel and seafood in a baked pasta dish appears in multiple Italian regional cookbooks from the late twentieth century. This recipe synthesises the standard approach.

recipe.freezeNotes: Not recommended: the seafood texture degrades significantly on freezing and reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled the day before and refrigerated unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the baking time if cooking from cold.

content.text: Seafood lasagne is a proper occasion dish. It is not quick, but it is not complicated: you make a cream-enriched béchamel, arrange layers of pasta and seafood, and bake. The key is not overcooking the seafood before it goes into the dish; it will continue to cook in the oven, and prawns especially turn rubbery if they are already fully cooked when they go in.

items.prepNote: fresh if possible; no-cook dried lasagne sheets work well
skinned, pin-boned, cut into 3 cm cubes

content.text: Melt the butter in a large, heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and stir into a paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, to remove the raw flour taste.

Add the white wine and stir vigorously. Gradually add the hot milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened. Add the cream, half the Parmesan, and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Spread a thin layer of béchamel across the base of a large, deep baking dish.

Layer pasta sheets over the béchamel. Arrange a third of the prawns, crab, and salmon chunks evenly over the pasta. Spoon a quarter of the remaining béchamel over the seafood. Repeat this layering twice more, ending with a top layer of pasta.
Pour the remaining béchamel over the top layer of pasta. Scatter the remaining Parmesan evenly over the surface.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and the lasagne is bubbling at the edges. Leave to rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

items.cause: Prawns pre-cooked before assembly, or baked too long
items.fix: Use raw prawns and do not pre-cook them. 40 to 45 minutes in the oven is enough to cook them through from raw.

items.cause: Béchamel too thin, or seafood released liquid during baking
items.fix: Make the béchamel thick enough to coat a spoon heavily. Pat the salmon dry before assembly.

content.text: Seafood lasagne is a dish of the Italian coast: Campania, Calabria, Sardinia, and the Adriatic ports where mixed seafood is abundant. It appears on Italian restaurant menus in London, Sydney, and New York as a special-occasion pasta dish. It is the kind of lasagne that does not have a ragù: the sauce is cream-based, the seafood is the point, and the pasta is the structure. It is best served once only; it does not reheat as gracefully as the meat version.
